test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who among the following was the first political leader in India to openly put forward, in his newspaper Bande Mataram, the idea of complete independence for the country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Aurobindo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sri Aurobindo** was the first political leader in India who openly advocated for **complete independence** through his writings in the newspaper **Bande Mataram**.
 
• The newspaper **Bande Mataram** was established in **1905**, during the period of the **Swadeshi Movement** against the partition of Bengal.
 
• **Sri Aurobindo** used Bande Mataram as a medium to propagate nationalist ideas and advocate for freedom from British rule, marking a significant departure from the moderate demands of early Indian leaders. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• His vision of **Purna Swaraj (complete independence)** was revolutionary at a time when most leaders were seeking dominion status or reforms under British governance.
 
• **Bande Mataram** played a key role in inspiring revolutionary sentiments and fostering a strong sense of nationalism among Indians. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sri Aurobindo's Contributions:**

 
 
• **Sri Aurobindo** was a prominent leader in the **Indian nationalist movement** before he moved towards spirituality.
 
• He played a significant role in transforming the **Indian freedom struggle** from a moderate phase to a more radical and revolutionary approach.
 
• His writings and speeches in the **Bande Mataram newspaper** inspired many revolutionaries and shaped the **early ideals of independence**.
 
 
 
• **Bande Mataram:**
 
 
• The newspaper was published in **English** and became a strong medium for spreading nationalist ideas across the country.
 
• It was one of the most influential publications during the **Swadeshi Movement** and was closely associated with revolutionary leaders like **Sri Aurobindo**.
 
• The name "Bande Mataram" was derived from the **nationalist song** written by **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee**, which also inspired the freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda:** While he advocated for the awakening of India and inspired nationalist sentiments, he did not explicitly call for complete independence through a publication. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:** He was a prominent figure in India's cultural renaissance but did not openly propagate complete independence in his writings. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:** He advocated for independence later in his political career, but he was not the first to call for complete independence in a publication. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline of Purna Swaraj:**

 
 
• **1905:** Sri Aurobindo’s writings in **Bande Mataram** openly advocated for complete independence.
 
• **1929:** The Indian National Congress passed the **Purna Swaraj resolution**, declaring complete independence as its goal.
 
 
 
• **Role of Revolutionary Publications:**
 
 
• Newspapers like **Bande Mataram** were instrumental in spreading revolutionary ideas and inspiring the youth during the freedom struggle.
 
• They served as platforms for leaders like **Sri Aurobindo** to articulate their vision of an independent India.
